data.body:
**Fresh measurement of the drift, plus a workaround that unblocks closes today.**

Measured 2026-09-20 on the live box (`i-00880b2c7f13527c5`), inside the `rebar-mcp-bd8c1c4ced77-8093` container:

```
git -C /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code log -1  -> 8f7417079a 2026-09-19 02:18:15 +0000 Restore Bedrock spend cap Terraform
git -C /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code rev-parse origin/main -> bd8c1c4ced77e86732dfc58ee9096f37434d889f
```

**The remote-tracking ref is current; only the checkout is stale.** `origin/main` in that workspace is exactly the tip of `main` (`bd8c1c4ced7`, 2026-09-20 06:47 UTC). The working tree sits at `8f7417079a`, an ancestor, **28.5 hours behind**. So the workspace does fetch — it never fast-forwards the local branch, which narrows the fix: the gap is the checkout step, not connectivity or credentials.

**Confirmed false FAIL.** Closing `ritzy-rancour-rat` (54c7-c5b1) failed completion verification 2 times with 3 unmet criteria, reporting:

> Line 4 of `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` still contains the string "two containers" … The fix has not landed in the working tree.

That is true of `8f7417079a` and false of `main`. `git show bd8c1c4ced7:infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` reads "Runs four containers on the AL2023 arm64 box" and names all four services at lines 5-6.

**Note the failure mode is confidently wrong, not merely unhelpful.** The finding asserts the fix "has not landed" and names the very commit it is blind to. An agent reading it at face value concludes its merged change was lost and re-does landed work — which is what happened here before the workspace was inspected directly.

**Workaround: pass `ref=origin/main` explicitly.** The `ref` parameter IS honoured; the default just resolves to the stale local branch. Same ticket, same session, no code change:

- `ref` omitted → FAIL, 3 unmet criteria
- `ref="main"` → FAIL, 3 unmet criteria (this names the *local* stale branch, so it is not a workaround)
- `ref="origin/main"` → **PASS**, closed with `completion_signature: {signed: true, cause: "signed"}`

An abbreviated SHA is rejected outright — `cannot resolve ref 'bd8c1c4ced7' to a commit in '/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code'` — so `origin/main` is the practical escape hatch until the refresh lands.

**Suggested acceptance criterion:** whatever refreshes the workspace, assert that a gate run with no explicit `ref` verifies the same tree as one with `ref=origin/main`. That is the invariant that broke here, and it is checkable without reproducing the 28-hour drift.
